column2: 1.1 Policy framework

Is there a national open data policy in your country and, if your country is an EU Member State, does this include a national legislation for the transposition of the Open Data Directive?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide (1) the URL and (2) title of the policy document and (3) briefly describe.
* If ‘other’, please provide (1) a brief explanation to support your answer choice and (2) provide the URL and indicate the policy section which explicitly references open data.
column4: Transposition of 2nd version of the PSI (3rd version in progress) https://www.ejustice.just.fgov.be/eli/loi/2016/05/04/2016009236/justel  (Loi relative à la réutilisation des informations du secteur public)
column7: The law (https://www.ejustice.just.fgov.be/eli/loi/2016/05/04/2016009236/justel) has been updated to transpose the 3rd version of the EU PSI/Open Data Directive

column2:

For Explanation:

* If 'not applicable', please provide (1) a brief explanation to support your answer choice and provide (2) the URL and indicate the policy section which explicitly references objectives, actions/measures, delivery timelines etc.
column4: https://data.gov.be/sites/default/files/public/content/compressed_fr-strategisch-dossier.pdf, focus on "open by default", economic aspects, and interaction with the community
column7: The 2015 document has not yet been updated (draft of new strategy in preparation)

For Explanation:

column4: E.g. Flanders Region, part of the general data strategy: https://www.vlaanderen.be/digitaal-vlaanderen/vlaamse-digitale-strategie/vlaamse-datastrategie
column7:
Flanders Region: https://www.vlaanderen.be/digitaal-vlaanderen/vlaamse-digitale-strategie/vlaamse-datastrategie, Vlaamse Data Strategie, focus on data awareness / ecosystem and governance / quality. 
Walloon Region: part of https://www.wallonie.be/sites/default/files/2021-10/plan_de_relance_de_la_wallonie_octobre_2021.pdf, Plan de Relance de la Wallonie (projects 139 - develop and govern open data, 297 - data centric approach, 298 - operalization of open data)

column2:
Does the national strategy/policy mandate carrying out and maintaining a data inventory by public bodies, whether at national or local level?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly specify.
column4: Mandatory publication on the federal open data portal
column7: Required by law to have the (meta)data published on the federal portal, art 17. Also, all the 3 Regions maintain and encourage or mandate publication on their portal(s)

column2:
Do these data inventories include the data collected by public bodies that cannot be published as open data (e.g. in relation to the EU Data Governance Act (EU) 2022/868)? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly specify.
column4: Some data repositories harvested by the federal open data portal do contain data sets that are not open data (eg geo.be in relation to INSPIRE and transportdata.be in relation to ITS)
column7: In addition to geo.be, also the regional MetaWal, Vlaamse Datavindplaats and DataStore Brussels contain INSPIRE (or other) datasets that are not necessarily open data

column2: 1.2 Governance of open data

Is there a governance structure in place that enables the participation and/or inclusion of various open data stakeholders? 

For Explanation:
*  If yes, please briefly describe the governance structure and its operating model
column4: new question
column7:
At federal level there is an open data task force and "FedAX" network of CDOs + informal meetings with members of the "OpenKnowledge Foundation" + by allowing anyone to request access to datasets, similar initiatives/governance at regional level
At Walloon Level, this is carried out by the SPW

column2:
How would you classify the model used for governing open data in your country? 

For Explanation:
*  Please briefly explain why this model was chosen/works best for your country
column4: practical considerations: sometimes demand for opening up data comes top-down, sometimes driven bottom-up, and so is the structure of the governance + political landscape with strong Regions and projects by larger cities

column2:
Does the governance structure ensure that the local and regional open data initiatives are facilitated and supported at national level?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please give an example of what kind of support.
* If not applicable, please explain why.
column4: new question
column7: While there are cooperations on open data initiatives and projects between federal/regional/local administrations, due to the political landscape, the federal level has no authority over open data projects on regional level

column2:
To what degree do local/regional public bodies conduct open data initiatives? 

For Explanation:
* If not applicable, please explain why.
column4: All 3 Regions have open data initiatives + a few larger cities (smaller cities require support of Regional level)

column2:
Is a document describing the responsibilities and governance structure of the national (and/or regional/local) open data team publicly available?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide the URL where this information is published.
column4: Explained in Royal Decree, chapitre 4 (https://www.ejustice.just.fgov.be/eli/arrete/2019/06/02/2019013333/justel#LNK0004)
column7: In addition to the answer from 2023, at the Walloon Region the structure of the regional team is also mentioned in a Decree (https://wallex.wallonie.be/eli/loi-decret/2022/11/24/2022207332)

column2:
Is there a regular exchange of knowledge or experiences between the national open data team and the team maintaining the national portal? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe how this exchange takes place and provide evidence supporting your answer (e.g. meeting agendas, URLs to news items).
column4: Same team: Maintainers of the data portal (open data task force) is also part of Transparency Committee
column7: Open Data Taskforce team is also member of the FedAx CDO Network, but the CDO meeting agendas/reports etc are not public

column2:
Does the governance model include the appointment of official roles in civil services that are dedicated to open data (e.g. open data officers)?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please describe how this task is fulfilled at public body level.
column4: "open data champion" role per federal public service, responsible for the development of an open data strategy within their administration + participate in transparency committee
column7: While the role is still in the 2015 open data strategy, nowadays the focus is more on Chief Data Officers (not all public services have this role) who happen to also manage open data (but also DGA data and non-open data / GDPR …)

column2:
Is there a regular exchange of knowledge or experiences between the national open data team and the wider network of open data officers in your country? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe how this exchange takes place and provide evidence supporting your answer (e.g. meeting agendas, URLs to news items).
column4: About 3 meetings / year with open data portal owners (local/regional/federal level): https://data.gov.be/fr/dcat-groupe-de-travail

column2:
Is there a regular exchange of knowledge or experiences between public sector bodies (i.e. the providers) and open data reusers (e.g. academia, citizens, businesses)?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe how this exchange takes place and provide evidence supporting your answer (e.g. meeting agendas, URLs to news items).
column4: Participation in yearly open data event "OpenBelgium" (https://2022.openbelgium.be/), and 1-to-1 (private) online meetings with small companies / NPOs and ICT sector federation Agoria
column7: In addition to the answer from 2023: Brussels Regions organizes "DataStore User Club" events (https://be.brussels/fr/propos-de-la-region/publications-open-data-statistiques/publications/publications-paradigm/users-club-datastore-lecoute-des-utilisateurs)  ,the Flanders Region organizes "Geo and Open Data Partner days" (https://www.wvigisco.be/event/partnerdag-geo-en-open-data/), exchange between National Geographic Institute and ODECO students (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/liubov-pilshchikova_odeco-training-week-at-ku-leuven-is-underway-activity-7186466881967411200-A1e5/)

column2:
Are there any processes in place to assess if public sector bodies are charging for data above marginal cost? (please see directive (EU) 2019/1024 on open data and the reuse of public sector information).

For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify the process(es).
column4: If a federal public body wants to publish data with additional constraints, including costs, the motivation and details have to be sent to the open data taskforce for advice. Art 7, Royal Decree https://www.ejustice.just.fgov.be/eli/loi/2016/05/04/2016009236/justel

column2:
What are the top 3 challenges that your country is facing in the implementation of the mentioned open data policies/strategy?

For Explanation:
* Please briefly describe.
column4: 1) Chicken-and-egg-problem (businesses want "as much data as possible" before they can prove their idea works, public services have limited resources and need to know what to prioritize first + are looking for examples to justify their efforts), 2) Somewhat overlapping data initiatives and regulations (e.g. INSPIRE, ITS,Europeana, PSI... have slightly different goals) , 3) Finding recurring budget for a few high value datasets (maps, historical weather data),

column2:
Are there activities in place to address these challenges in your country (e.g. with specific national/regional/local plans or initiatives)?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the measures that you have adopted or plan to adopt to address these challenges. 
* If no, please specifiy what is hampering finding a strategic approach to solve these challenges.
column4: On chicken and egg problem: projects like combined address register with (also) clear benefits for administrations as a "teaser" to encourage administrations to publish more data

column2:
Are there any activities in place to assist data holders with publishing their data as open data (i.e. to help them with the data opening process)?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please describe/provide examples of these activities.
column4: new question
column7:
Support from FPS BOSA, especially on publishing and converting metadata, but also advise on choosing a license, formats / use cases …
Support at Regional Level (eg SPW support administrations in Walloon Region, Paradigm for the Brussels Region, and DigitaalVlaanderen for the Flanders Region)

column2:
Is there a professional development or training plan for civil servants working with data in your country? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe these training activities.
column4:
At the national level, there are sessions (https://data.gov.be/fr/news/seance-dinformation-donnees-ouvertes-services-federaux) and trainings on data in general (though not part of a specific data track) like satellite data (https://terrascope.be/en/news-events/register-our-new-terrascope-webinars) which are open to servants and private sector.
At the regional level, there are trainings, e.g.http://www.futurocite.be/ouvrirmaville/ouvrir-ma-ville-2023/
column7: In addition to the answer of previous year: 2024 edition of Ouvrir Ma Ville (Walloon Region, https://www.futurocite.be/ouvrirmaville/), Smart Flanders "Open Data Lokale Besturen" trainings for (local) administrations (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RpzHdTtY1TE)

column7: This years editions: https://terrascope.be/en/news-events/terrascope-webinars, https://osoc.be/, https://www.citizensofwallonia.be/, https://openstreetmap.be/en/category/event.html, and DataBusters (https://www.futurocite.be/databusters-appli-chasseurs-donnees/)
